correctness.rationale: For each period-n word with m zero symbols, commuting diagonal multiplication yields exponent gap (2t/n)|m−phi(n−m)|. Equality would require m/n=1/phi, impossible since the golden ratio is irrational. The choice 2phi*t<−alpha*log(theta) gives one-step fiber bunching (and hence strong bunching in dimension two). The Bernoulli measure with zero frequency 1/phi gives exact zero exponents on both coordinate axes, violating the uniform gap necessary for domination. Irrational rational approximants provide periodic gaps tending to zero. Verified symbolic arithmetic and a supplementary length≤39 numerical nonvanishing check; latter is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A concise and explicit boundary example for whether a uniform periodic spectral-gap hypothesis can be weakened to pointwise strictness, with the lowest fiber dimension and the extra strong-bunching and near-identity constraints. The zero-gap invariant measure exposes why the periodic quantifier needs uniformity. The construction is reducible; neither classification nor strong irreducibility is claimed.

limitations: Excludes strongly irreducible cocycles and any classification of the full nondominated locus.
